newsitem.title: NORWAY: Palestinian hijacker may serve term in Norway jail.
newsitem.headline: Palestinian hijacker may serve term in Norway jail.

text.p: Norway said on Tuesday a convicted Palestinian hijacker, who had lived in the Nordic country with her family, may serve her 12-year prison term in a Norwegian jail with approval from the German court that sentenced her.

Souhaila Andrawes, who was sentenced by a Hamburg court on Tuesday for her part in the 1977 hijacking of a Lufthansa passenger jet to Somalia and the murder of its pilot, has said she would like to serve her term in Norway.
Andrawes moved to Norway in 1991 under a false name and was extradited to Germany last year after her identity became known, leaving her husband and daughter behind in Oslo.
"The convict may apply to be transferred to Norway if she wants to," a Norwegian justice ministry spokesman said. "If Germany approves of it, we will not raise any objections."
The prosecution had asked for a 12-year sentence, rejecting Andrawes's assertion that she was not responsible for shooting the pilot as it was the gang leader who pulled the trigger.
She is the only survivor of a group of four Palestinians, who hijacked the German airline's plane to press their demands for the release of fellow guerrillas in jail.
